message.content: {"executive_summary":"This evacuation experiment deployed 100 homogeneous agents on a 38×38 interior grid with a single 3-cell door and ran for the full 300-step time cap without early termination. All agents moved eastward at a fixed speed under a block-on-collision rule, producing a conspicuous, self-organized queue immediately upstream of the door. Despite agents steadily passing through the aperture, at least one remained inside when the clock expired.\n\nThe available evidence is purely configurational and endpoint-status based: no per-step evacuation counts, density heatmaps, or flow rates were logged. Consequently, we can qualitatively describe the bottleneck dynamics and spatial clustering at the door, but cannot quantify evacuation rates, congestion duration, or the effects of agent decision policies driven by the LLM components.","conclusions":["A single narrow (3-cell) exit generates a persistent high-density queue and classic bottleneck behavior under uniform movement rules.","Collision blocking enforces a self-organized, single-file queue; no off-path clusters or territorial subgroups emerged.","The run’s 300-step completion without full evacuation indicates door capacity is insufficient for timely egress of 100 agents at the given speed.","Lack of logged time-series data prevents calculation of key metrics: per-step throughput, evacuation curves, and density profiles.","Emergent phenomena (queue formation and decongestion waves) can be identified qualitatively but not measured or linked to agent decision‐making policies.","Uniform agent speed and deterministic movement amplify congestion; no heterogeneity was present to test alternate flow dynamics."],"recommendations":["Instrument the model to record per-step evacuated_count and in-room population to build evacuation time-series curves.","Log door throughput and local density heatmaps each step to quantify bottleneck severity and clearance rates.","Run sensitivity tests on door width and number of exits (e.g., 4-cell door, two doors) to assess impact on total evacuation time.","Introduce agent heterogeneity in speed or decision rules (e.g., randomized wait times or LLM-suggested rerouting) to evaluate strategies for smoother flow.","Integrate checkpoints to record individual waiting times at the bottleneck, enabling evaluation of service fairness and delay distribution.","In future experiments, enable dynamic environmental feedback (e.g., signage or audible cues) to test adaptive decision-making policies and their effect on congestion mitigation."]}
